title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 408
paragraphs: When the Persians had marched all the way through the waterless region and were encamped near the Egyptians intending to join battle, the foreign mercenaries of the Egyptian king, who were Greeks and Carians, holding a grudge against Phanes because he had brought a foreign-speaking army against Egypt, contrived against him as follows: Phanes had children whom he had left behind in Egypt. These they brought to their camp into the sight of their father, and they set up a mixing-bowl between the two camps. Then they brought up the children one by one and cut their throats so that the blood ran into the bowl. When they had gone through every one of the children, they brought wine and water and poured them into the bowl, and only after all the mercenaries had drunk of the blood did they join battle. Then, after a battle fought with great stubbornness in which very many fell on both sides, the Egyptians at length turned and fled.
